reason: The text contains numerous regular, non-divine characters who demonstrate clear agency and make autonomous decisions. Examples include: (1) the Hebrew midwives Shiphrah and Puah, who fear God and actively refuse Pharaoh's command to kill male infants; (2) Moses' mother, who hides her son and places him in a basket, making deliberate choices to preserve his life; (3) Pharaoh's daughter, who decides to save the Hebrew child; (4) Miriam, who acts as a lookout and later leads the women in celebration; (5) the general Israelite population, who complain, gather food, and quarrel with their leaders; (6) Joshua, who is chosen and acts independently in battle; (7) Jethro, who observes events and provides counsel; (8) Pharaoh's Egyptian servants, who urge Pharaoh to release the Israelites; and (9) various ordinary people of Egypt who experience fear and give goods to the departing Israelites. These characters are not merely passive recipients of events; they make choices, take initiatives, and respond to circumstances based on their own values and judgments.
